title: Kenya and DR Congo agree to bring back ambassadors after Ruto-Tshisekedi talks in Oyo
key_points: Ruto and DR Congo's President Tshisekedi met in Oyo, Republic of the Congo, on Sunday, November 22.
They agreed to work towards full diplomatic ties, including the return of ambassadors. No date has been given.
The two countries have had no ambassadors in each other's capitals for years, after a row over the M23-linked AFC alliance launched in Nairobi in December 2023.
At home on Tuesday, Ruto said the Hustler Fund will get Ksh5 billion more and some borrowing limits will rise.
content:
Kenya and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) have agreed to repair their broken relationship. President William Ruto and DRC President Felix Tshisekedi met on Sunday, November 22, in Oyo, a town in the Republic of the Congo. They agreed to work towards full diplomatic ties, including bringing back ambassadors.

Who brought them together

The talks were hosted by Republic of the Congo President Denis Sassou N'Guesso. Togo's leader, Faure Gnassingbé, who is the African Union's mediator for eastern DRC, helped lead the talks. Ruto cut short his tour of Western Kenya to travel to Oyo, Dawan Africa and Xinhua reported.

What went wrong between the two countries

The trouble started in December 2023. A new political and military alliance, the Congo River Alliance (AFC), was launched in Nairobi. The AFC is linked to the M23 rebels who fight the Congolese army in eastern DRC. Kinshasa was angry and recalled its ambassador from Kenya, according to Xinhua and Uganda's The Independent.

Relations got worse after that. In January 2025, rioters in Kinshasa attacked and looted the Kenyan embassy, Kenyans.co.ke reported. The DRC also did not accept Kenya's chosen ambassador, Peter Tum. In October 2025, Nairobi hosted Congolese opposition figures, including former president Joseph Kabila. Kenya said it could not stop people from expressing political views.

What they agreed

According to a joint statement reported by several outlets, the two leaders agreed to:

  • work towards full diplomatic relations, including the return of ambassadors;
  • restart their Joint Grand Commission for Cooperation and hold regular talks;
  • solve differences through dialogue and respect each other's borders and independence;
  • grow trade, investment and security cooperation;
  • work together on stopping Ebola.

Ruto said the two countries had agreed to "open a new chapter", Dawan Africa reported. The DRC presidency said on X that the leaders agreed to fully restore relations, notably through the return of their ambassadors, according to Xinhua.

Outlets used slightly different words. Citizen Digital said the leaders agreed to "work towards" restoring ambassadors, while Xinhua said they agreed to "fully restore" ties. No outlet has reported a date for the ambassadors to return. Kenya's foreign ministry has not given further details in the reports we saw.

Why it matters

The DRC is a big trade partner for Kenya and a member of the East African Community (EAC). Many Kenyan traders, truck drivers and businesses work in eastern DRC. Better ties could make trade and travel easier. The two countries also share the fight against Ebola in the region.

Also in Kenya politics on Tuesday

Hustler Fund: Speaking at State House, Nairobi, at a Joyful Women Organisation (JOYWO) event, Ruto said the government will add Ksh5 billion to the Hustler Fund. He said more than 4.5 million borrowers will move to a bridge loan of up to Ksh150,000, and those stuck at a Ksh10,000 limit will get higher limits if they repay, Kenyans.co.ke reported.

Malala stays with DCP: Cleophas Malala, deputy leader of Rigathi Gachagua's DCP party, denied reports that he has joined Senator Edwin Sifuna's Linda Mwananchi Movement or is running for Nairobi governor. He said he is still running for Kakamega governor on a DCP ticket, according to Kenyans.co.ke.
